gaps.sentence: There's no point ___ about it now.
gaps.explanation: there's no point + -ing: no point worrying.

gaps.sentence: I remembered ___ the door, so I went back to check.
gaps.explanation: remember + -ing = recall a past action; remember to do = not forget a duty.

gaps.sentence: The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: She couldn't resist ___ the last biscuit.
I can't stand ___ kept waiting when I have an appointment.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't stand' takes a gerund; the passive gerund is 'being kept'.
would rather takes the bare infinitive: I'd rather stay.

gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the deadline despite the strike.
